BackendConfig.description: One `[backends.<name>]` table (D-P5-10, D-P5-15). Typed options only: no free-form map.

base_url.description: The address of the server, for example `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` for a local server. Required unless `preset` supplies it. Use `https` unless the host is a loopback address. It must not carry a user name, a password, a query or a fragment.
base_url.title: Base Url

key_env.description: The NAME of the environment variable that holds the API key, for example `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`: upper-case letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit. Empty when the server needs no key. A preset fills it when this table leaves it out. The key itself is never written in this file.
key_env.title: Key Env

kind.description: `openai-compatible` for a server that speaks the OpenAI chat API: a local server or a hosted provider. `anthropic` for Claude, through Anthropic's Messages API.
kind.title: Kind

model.description: The model name the server expects, for example `qwen3.5:4b`.
model.title: Model

preset.description: A named hosted provider. It fills `base_url`, `key_env`, `structured_output` and `temperature` when this table leaves them out. Not allowed with `kind = "anthropic"`.
preset.title: Preset

reasoning.description: The reasoning effort the server should use: `off`, `low`, `medium` or `high`. `unset` sends no reasoning setting. Not allowed with `kind = "anthropic"`.
reasoning.title: Reasoning

request_timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for one answer from this backend, from 1 to 3600. Unset means this table sets no request timeout.
request_timeout_s.title: Request Timeout S

retry.description: The `[backends.<name>.retry.<layer>]` tables: retry layers for the seats that use this backend, between a seat's own override and `[retry]`.

structured_output.description: How the server is asked for structured output. `json_schema`: the server enforces the output schema. `json_object`: the server returns any JSON object, and MineWorld checks it against the schema. `none`: no structured-output request is sent.
structured_output.title: Structured Output

temperature.description: `send` sends the sampling temperature with each request. `omit` leaves it out, for a model that refuses a temperature.
temperature.title: Temperature

BackendConfig.title: BackendConfig

BudgetConfig.description: The `[budgets]` table: the limits of `BudgetPolicy`, and where the spend is kept.

call_timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for one model call before it is abandoned.
call_timeout_s.title: Call Timeout S

calls_per_wall_hour.description: The most model calls one person's seat may make in any rolling hour of real time. Real time is wall-clock seconds, not simulated days.
calls_per_wall_hour.title: Calls Per Wall Hour

ledger.description: A SQLite file that keeps the spend, so a restart neither resets it nor counts a call twice. Unset keeps the spend in memory only. A relative path is resolved against this configuration file.
ledger.title: Ledger

max_in_flight.description: The most model calls that may run at the same time in this process.
max_in_flight.title: Max In Flight

tokens_per_wall_day.description: The most tokens one seat may use in any rolling 24 hours of real time.
tokens_per_wall_day.title: Tokens Per Wall Day

BudgetConfig.title: BudgetConfig

ControllerConfig.description: The `[controller]` table: the consult's bounds and the seat's timing (pr-s10-p6 §5.13).

consult_deadline_s.description: Wall seconds from a trigger's receipt to the submit, from 1 to 120.
consult_deadline_s.title: Consult Deadline S

greet_cooldown_s.description: World seconds before the same person may trigger a greeting again, from 0 to 86400.
greet_cooldown_s.title: Greet Cooldown S

handback_s.description: Wall seconds a seat stays with its fallback model after a handback, from 1 to 600.
handback_s.title: Handback S

max_calls.description: The most model calls one consult may make, from 1 to 10.
max_calls.title: Max Calls

recall_episodes.description: How many episode lines of memory a consult shows, from 0 to 8.
recall_episodes.title: Recall Episodes

seat_retry_s.description: Wall seconds between joins while another client holds the seat, from 1 to 3600.
seat_retry_s.title: Seat Retry S

ControllerConfig.title: ControllerConfig

ControllerOverrides.description: The same keys as `[controller]`, each optional: a `[seat_overrides.<key>.controller]` table.
ControllerOverrides.title: ControllerOverrides

LayerConfig.description: One retry layer or the breaker: a policy id and its parameters (checked by its registry, C7/C8).

parameters.description: The policy's parameters. The policy checks them; an unknown one is refused by name.
parameters.title: Parameters

policy.description: The policy's id, one of the installed policies (for example `exponential-backoff`).
policy.title: Policy

LayerConfig.title: LayerConfig

RecordingConfig.description: The `[recording]` table: where answers come from, and whether they are recorded.

cassette.description: The cassette file, which `record` writes and `replay` reads. Required for `record` and `replay`. A relative path is resolved against this configuration file.
cassette.title: Cassette

mode.description: Where answers come from. `live`: the configured backend answers. `record`: the backend answers and each answer is written to the cassette. `replay`: answers are read from the cassette, and no network client is built. `scripted`: a backend supplied in code, for tests.
mode.title: Mode

RecordingConfig.title: RecordingConfig

RetryConfig.description: The three retry layers of one table: `[retry]`, `[retry.<layer>]` per table.

content.description: The content layer (invalid answers, re-asked); unset uses the bundled default.

semantic.description: The semantic layer (refused proposals, re-planned); unset uses the bundled default.

transport.description: The transport layer (backoff, Retry-After); unset uses the bundled default.

RetryConfig.title: RetryConfig

SeatOverrides.description: A `[seat_overrides.<key>]` table: per-seat controller bounds and per-seat retry layers (D-P6b-3).

controller.description: The `[seat_overrides.<key>.controller]` table: the seat's own bounds.

retry.description: The `[seat_overrides.<key>.retry.<layer>]` tables: the seat's own retry layers.

SeatOverrides.title: SeatOverrides

SecretsConfig.description: The `[secrets]` table: an optional `.env`-style file that holds API keys.

env_file.description: A `.env`-style file that holds API keys, read only when named here. A relative path is resolved against this configuration file. On macOS and Linux the file must not be readable by its group or by others (`chmod 600`); the loader refuses it otherwise.
env_file.title: Env File

SecretsConfig.title: SecretsConfig

description: The whole `cognition.toml` file: one table per section below, and the backends it names.

backends.description: The `[backends.<name>]` tables: one per backend, named by you. A name uses lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, and does not start or end with `-` or `_`.
backends.title: Backends

breaker.description: The `[breaker]` table: the per-seat circuit breaker. Unset uses the bundled default.

budgets.description: The `[budgets]` table: the most calls and tokens the client may spend.

controller.description: The `[controller]` table: the consult's bounds and the seat's timing.

decisions_json.description: The JSON that `mineworld decisions … --json` printed for the world the server runs. A relative path is resolved against this configuration file.
decisions_json.title: Decisions Json

invite_env.description: The NAME of the environment variable that holds the server's invite. The invite is read from the environment only; this file never holds it.
invite_env.title: Invite Env

nickname.description: The nickname the controller joins with, from 1 to 32 characters.
nickname.title: Nickname

recording.description: The `[recording]` table. Required: it names the mode every answer comes from.

retry.description: The `[retry]` table: the three retry layers of every seat (`[retry.<layer>]`).

seat_overrides.description: The `[seat_overrides.<key>]` tables: per-seat controller bounds and retry layers. The name `seat_overrides` is used so that `seats` can name the subset of seats (D-P6b-3).
seat_overrides.title: Seat Overrides

seats.description: Optional subset of the `lm` seats in `decisions_json` to join. Every entry must be an `lm` seat of that file; unset joins all of them.
seats.title: Seats

secrets.description: The `[secrets]` table: where API keys are read from.

server.description: The protocol address of the server, for example `ws://127.0.0.1:7878/ws`. Required by the LM controller (`python -m mineworld_cognition`); a loopback address is the usual choice.
server.title: Server

store.description: The directory of the controller's own state (memory stores, resume secrets, decision logs). A relative path is resolved against this configuration file. It must not be inside a world.
store.title: Store

tiers.description: The `[tiers]` table: which backend answers each decision tier. Keys are tier names (`ordinary_decision`, `social`, `major_decision`, `summarize`; their meaning is in ARCHITECTURE.md §9.1). Values are a backend name from `[backends.<name>]`, or `none` for a tier that uses no model. A tier left out uses no model, the same as `none`.
tiers.title: Tiers
